description: Automerge is the default posture here, not the exception. This repo is a design catalog with no downstream consumers: nothing depends on its artifacts, so a bad bump costs a revert, not a broken release. What stops a bad bump reaching main is the `Protect Main` ruleset — CI (build + discovery, unit tests, ktfmtCheck, catalog spec, catalog spec) is required, and `platformAutomerge` hands the merge to GitHub's own auto-merge, which only fires once those checks pass. Set the ruleset up with `scripts/setup-repo-protection.sh`; without it, automerge silently degrades to merging as soon as Renovate can, which is not what any of this intends.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. A major on Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform or the preview toolchain changes what the catalog renders, and the render is the product — a human looks at the visual diff before it lands. Also hold a major for two weeks so the ecosystem's first round of regressions surfaces on someone else's CI.
Wear Compose and the mobile Compose BOM decide how every sticker in the catalog is laid out, and the render is the product — so they land as one PR whose visual diff is the review, not on automerge.

Horologist is the catalog's SECOND component library (see AGENTS.md) and it ships its artifacts as one release — media-ui-material3, auth-composables-material3, compose-layout, images-base and the models they take all move together, and a skew between them is a compile error at best. Group them into one PR. Not automerged, for the same reason Compose is not: these draw the media player, the sign-in screens and the fast-scrolling list, and the render is the product — a human reads the visual diff. They are on an alpha line, so expect the diff to be real.

Toolchain and CI plumbing — the Gradle wrapper, the GitHub Actions pins and the pinned Node version. These are judged entirely by whether CI passes, which is the one thing automerge already waits for, so batch them into a single weekly PR rather than one PR per action. Deliberately BEFORE the compose-ai-tools rule, which re-claims its own action ref out of this batch — that pin travels with the Gradle coords, not with the weekly plumbing.

LAST ON PURPOSE. Renovate applies packageRules in order and the LAST match wins, so while this rule sat above the CI-toolchain rule the pinned `compose-ai-tools` action ref — a github-actions dependency — was pulled back out of this group into the weekly batch, and the two halves of one release drifted apart exactly as the rule below says they must not (compose-ai-tools#4220 found the pin three releases behind the Gradle coords). Keep this rule below the CI-toolchain one. It is the BROAD rule for the ee.schimke.composeai group, and the only rules allowed after it are the four that carve their own trains back out of it — the compose-ai-tools DATA line, contracts, server and rc-players — because the last matching rule wins. The data line is the odd one: the other three are separate repositories, while it ships from THIS repository's own tags on a version line the release job decides independently, so "one release" below means the CORE line only. compose-ai-tools ships the preview CLI, the ee.schimke.composeai Gradle artifacts (the preview-annotations dependency and the ee.schimke.composeai.preview plugin marker) and the reusable CI actions/workflows as a single CORE release (the `data-*` runtime coordinates move on their own line — see the rule immediately below). Group the pinned action refs and the Gradle coords into ONE PR so the CLI, plugin and annotation pins can never skew apart — a skew breaks preview discovery outright. Track it aggressively and automerge once CI is green: the release moves several times a day and the pin is only useful if it keeps up. Republishing the catalog against the new renderer needs no extra step, because design-artifacts.yml has a push trigger on main covering the manifest paths this PR touches.

LAST-GROUP CARVE-OUT, like contracts / server / rc-players, for the line published from yschimke/compose-preview-daemon: `preview-annotations`, `data-preview-overrides-runtime` and `data-remotecompose-connector` moved there from compose-ai-tools in compose-ai-tools#5336 and release from its 3.0.0 on a version line of their own, which `composePreviewDaemon` in gradle/libs.versions.toml pins. They must not share the compose-ai-tools group: one group means one shared version ref, and a ref that spans two release lines is a version lie whichever way it points (#199, #347). This rule used to be the carve-out for compose-ai-tools' own DATA line and excluded 2.2.1 by name (that release's data POMs pinned a `daemon-core` that was never uploaded); the data line and the exclusion went with the move. Named by exact artifactId: `data-render-core`, `data-theme-core`, `data-layoutinspector-core` and `data-preview-overrides-core` are compose-preview-CONTRACTS coordinates and belong to the rule below. Automerged like its neighbours; CI is the check.

The wire contracts are published from yschimke/compose-preview-contracts on their OWN version line (2.x, against compose-ai-tools' 1.5x.x), so they are not part of the release above and must not share its group. This is the rc-players failure below in a second guise: one group means one shared version ref in gradle/libs.versions.toml, and Renovate raises that ref to whichever train released last, proposing a version the other never published. The shared preset already splits these trains; this rule exists to give the contracts the same aggressive posture as its neighbour, which a repo-local rule appended after the preset would otherwise drop back to the weekly default. Listed by exact artifactId because the two repos' names interleave: `daemon-protocol` is a contract, `daemon-core` is not.

`compose-preview serve` and its render host, published from yschimke/compose-preview-server on a third version line independent of both the tools and the contracts. Same reasoning as the contracts rule above. The catalog does not resolve these coordinates today; the rule is here so that the day it does, the coordinate lands in its own PR rather than being swallowed by the compose-ai-tools group above it. `compose-preview-ui-builder-export` is the coordinate this catalog DOES resolve, on its own `composePreviewServer` ref, and it was missing from the list — so it fell through to the broad compose-ai-tools rule above, the one thing every train rule here exists to prevent. The shared preset now names it too.

LAST, after the compose-ai-tools rule and the two train rules that follow it: the last match wins, so this rule takes the RemoteCompose players back out of that group. The patterns cover the whole rc-players train rather than only the `third-party-rc-embedded-player` coordinate this catalog resolves today: naming one coordinate left the rest falling back into the broad rule above, so the first player artifact added here would have inherited the very bug this rule exists to fix. They carry the ee.schimke.composeai GROUP, but are not part of that release — it is published from yschimke/rc-players on a version line of its own that is already ahead. Grouped, Renovate raised the shared `composePreviewAnnotations` ref to a player-only version and dragged four compose-ai-tools artifacts to a version nobody published, which is what broke #199. Ungrouped it moves on its own ref (`rcEmbeddedPlayer` in gradle/libs.versions.toml) in a PR of its own. Automerged like its neighbour and for the same reason: the connector resolves the player's entry point reflectively, so a skew shows up as the embedded lane going quiet, and the render CI is what catches that.
